items.title: Disable a KMS key and watch decryption stop
items.kills: "You can delete a KMS key at once, and a disabled key is gone."
items.cost: Close to $0. The key exists for less than one hour before you schedule its deletion, and AWS KMS prorates the key price hourly. The few requests of this task fall inside the AWS KMS free tier of 20,000 requests/month.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $1/month for the key, prorated hourly: about a thirtieth of $1 each day. Disabling the key does not stop this charge. Scheduling its deletion does.
items.read_only_alternative: Use this when you cannot create KMS keys. It changes nothing. List the aliases of your account in this Region: aws kms list-aliases --query "Aliases[].[AliasName,TargetKeyId]" An alias that starts with alias/aws/ and shows a key ID points to an AWS managed key. An alias without a key ID has no key yet. Use one key ID as <KEY_ID> and read who manages the key and its state: aws kms describe-key --key-id <KEY_ID> --query "KeyMetadata.[KeyManager,KeyState]" Expect AWS and Enabled. You cannot disable an AWS managed key or schedule its deletion, so the break-it step of this task needs a customer managed key.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Create a symmetric encryption KMS key with the two book tags. Name no key policy: the default key policy lets the IAM policies of your account allow the use of the key.
steps.command: aws kms create-key --description "saa kms-t01 practice key" --tags TagKey=book,TagValue=saa TagKey=task,TagValue=kms-t01
steps.expect: No output. KEY_ID now holds the key ID of the new key.

steps.text: Encrypt a short text with the new key. The value c2FhIHRlc3Q= is the text saa test in base64, the form that the AWS CLI expects for --plaintext.
steps.expect: No output. CIPHERTEXT now holds the encrypted text, also in base64.

steps.text: Decrypt the ciphertext while the key is enabled.
steps.expect: c2FhIHRlc3Q=, the base64 form of saa test.

steps.text: Disable the key. Disabling is the reversible way to stop all use of a key.
Read the state of the key.
steps.expect: Disabled and false. The key still exists.
An error that names DisabledException and says that the key is disabled.
steps.predict: Your IAM permissions did not change, and the ciphertext did not change. Does the decrypt call still work?
steps.explain: A disabled key works in no cryptographic operation [until you re-enable it](../facts/kms.md#kms-disabled-key-no-crypto-until-reenabled). Decrypt is a cryptographic operation, so the call fails although your permissions are the same. [Disabled keys continue to incur storage charges](../facts/kms.md#kms-disabled-keys-still-charged), so disabling a key does not stop its monthly fee.

steps.text: Fix it: enable the key again.
Decrypt the same ciphertext a third time.
steps.expect: c2FhIHRlc3Q= again. Nothing was lost while the key was disabled.

cleanup.text: Schedule the key for deletion with the shortest waiting period, 7 days. The output shows KeyState PendingDeletion and a DeletionDate: AWS KMS does not delete a key at once.

verify.expect: The ARN of this key, because a key that waits for deletion keeps its tags. The list is not the proof. For each ARN, run aws kms describe-key --key-id with that ARN and --query KeyMetadata.KeyState. PendingDeletion passes. Enabled or Disabled fails: the cleanup did not run, so schedule the deletion of that key.

still_costs: Nothing after the cleanup. A customer managed key that is scheduled for deletion is not charged. To check the key, run aws kms describe-key --key-id $KEY_ID --query "KeyMetadata.[KeyState,DeletionDate]" and expect PendingDeletion and a date 7 days from today.
If you cancel the deletion, the key is charged again as though it was never scheduled for deletion.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, KEY_ID is empty. Find the key ARN again with the verify command, and use the key ID at its end.

items.title: Rotate a KMS key and decrypt data from before the rotation
items.kills: "Rotation gives the key a new key ID, and old data must be re-encrypted."
items.cost: Close to $0. The key and its one rotation exist for less than one hour before you schedule the deletion, and AWS KMS prorates both charges hourly. The few requests fall inside the AWS KMS free tier of 20,000 requests/month.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $1/month for the key, $1/month more for the on-demand rotation of step 6, and $1/month more after the automatic rotation about 90 days later, all prorated hourly. The second rotation is the last one that adds cost. This runs until you schedule the deletion of the key.
items.read_only_alternative: Use this when you cannot create KMS keys. It changes nothing. List the aliases of your account in this Region: aws kms list-aliases --query "Aliases[].[AliasName,TargetKeyId]" Use the key ID of an alias that starts with alias/aws/ as <KEY_ID>. That key is an AWS managed key. Read its rotation status: aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <KEY_ID> Expect "KeyRotationEnabled": true. AWS rotates every AWS managed key each year, and you cannot turn that rotation off. Services keep using the same key ID after each rotation.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Create a symmetric encryption KMS key with the two book tags.
steps.command: aws kms create-key --description "saa kms-t02 practice key" --tags TagKey=book,TagValue=saa TagKey=task,TagValue=kms-t02
steps.expect: No output. KEY_ID now holds the key ID of the new key.

steps.text: Encrypt a short text before any rotation. The value c2FhIHRlc3Q= is the text saa test in base64, the form that the AWS CLI expects for --plaintext.
steps.expect: No output. CIPHERTEXT now holds the encrypted text.

steps.text: Read the rotation status of the new key: is automatic rotation on?
steps.expect: "KeyRotationEnabled": false. Automatic rotation of a new customer managed key stays off until you turn it on.

steps.text: Turn on automatic rotation with a rotation period of 90 days, the shortest period that AWS KMS accepts.

steps.expect: true, 90, and a date about 90 days from today.

steps.text: Do not wait 90 days: rotate the key material now, on demand. An on-demand rotation does not change the automatic rotation schedule.
steps.expect: The same key ID as in KEY_ID.

steps.text: List the completed rotations of the key.
steps.expect: ON_DEMAND and the date and time of today. If the list is empty, the rotation is still in progress: wait one minute and run the command again.

steps.text: Decrypt the ciphertext of step 2, made with the old key material. Does it decrypt, and under which key ID?
steps.expect: The ARN of the same key, which ends with the ID in KEY_ID, and c2FhIHRlc3Q=. The old ciphertext decrypts without re-encryption, and the key ID did not change.

cleanup.text: Schedule the key for deletion with the shortest waiting period, 7 days.

verify.expect: The ARN of this key, because a key that waits for deletion keeps its tags. The list is not the proof. For each ARN, run aws kms describe-key --key-id with that ARN and --query KeyMetadata.KeyState. PendingDeletion passes. Enabled or Disabled fails: the cleanup did not run, so schedule the deletion of that key.

still_costs: Nothing after the cleanup. A customer managed key that is scheduled for deletion is not charged. To check the key, run aws kms describe-key --key-id $KEY_ID --query "KeyMetadata.[KeyState,DeletionDate]" and expect PendingDeletion and a date 7 days from today.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, KEY_ID is empty. Find the key ARN again with the verify command, and use the key ID at its end.
